A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAPTURe study. All 15 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM evaluations, human counting results, and experiments with coordinate oracles, inpainting, temperature backoff, and model confidence.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of two VLMs and a chain-of-thought comparison.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, answer extraction, CountGD hybrid, coordinate oracles, inpainting pipeline, and temperature-backoff procedures are retained. Chain-of-thought is added as a supplementary comparison rather than a revision of the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 924 real images covering 92 object types and 1,250 synthetic images, with occluded and unoccluded conditions. The added model and prompting comparisons introduce no new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MiniCPM-o 2.6 and Kimi-VL-A3B alongside the original four VLMs. V2 Table 6 also compares GPT-4o and Qwen2VL with their CoT variants. Existing human, CountGD, hybrid, and auxiliary-information comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a CoT prompting condition involving examples for GPT-4o and Qwen2VL on the existing occluded datasets. Existing metrics, validation procedures, and stated token budgets remain unchanged. No changed human-study sampling protocol is documented despite Table 3's revised scores.

E4.justification: V2 adds one focused analysis testing whether CoT improves counting performance. Temperature backoff, occluded-only counting, confidence calibration, and number-bias analyses remain; the number-bias discussion moves from Section 4.2 into Appendix C.5.

E5.justification: Both versions estimate Qwen2VL confidence through direct prompting and 20 sampled responses per question, retaining the same reliability curves. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains the original four VLM rows and adds occluded real/synthetic sMAPE scores of 30.08/19.00 for MiniCPM-o and 25.96/18.07 for Kimi-VL. New CoT results show synthetic error changing from 9.71 to 7.73 for GPT-4o and 11.74 to 37.81 for Qwen2VL. Table 3 replaces all four VLM score pairs despite retaining its 100-example description. Section 4.1 also corrects GPT-4o's cited occluded synthetic error from 5.90 to 9.71.

T1.justification: The sMAPE definitions and dataset-filtering inequality are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an amodal-counting benchmark for spatial and world-model reasoning. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that VLMs struggle, humans perform well, and auxiliary information helps.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 newly interprets CoT as generally harmful and attributes a synthetic-setting exception to similarity between prompt examples and test items. Table 6 supports that exception for GPT-4o only. Existing explanations concerning occlusion, visual counting, and world modeling remain.

D1.justification: The token budgets, filtering threshold, answer-extraction details, prompt-selection procedure, Appendix D prompt texts, and code/data access information are retained. V2 provides no corresponding new prompt texts or execution settings for the added models and CoT comparison.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to the Kimi-VL technical report and MiniCPM-V paper. Section 5 adds an explicit claim that CAPTURe's combined requirements provide a stricter spatial-reasoning test than typical VQA; the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 tightens wording throughout, adds an Appendix C overview, adopts findings-based subsection headings, and consolidates number-bias discussion in Appendix C.5. These are limited editorial and organizational changes within the retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds the CoT table, expands Table 2, reorders the temperature-backoff table's columns, and expands the occluded-counting table with previously reported all-object scores and differences. Several tables, figures, and prompt boxes move; the underlying plotted results and overall visual design remain.

improvement.justification: The additional model comparisons and CoT analysis broaden the evidence, but reporting inconsistencies complicate the benefit. Table 3's revised VLM scores now match full-dataset Table 2 while the text still asserts a matched 100-example human comparison. Its new 14-times synthetic gap also disagrees with 14.19/0.92, approximately 15.4. Section 4.1 retains the old average occlusion penalties despite Table 2's expanded averages. Unclear provenance of the revised human-comparison scores prevents a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
